headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error if OCR output is fed into a prompt-leaking agent; other risks are limited by missing shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR can process documents/images and run browsers, so its outputs may contain attacker-controlled text. system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak oriented agent, but no shared channel is documented. Because a direct ingestion path is plausible yet unproven, I rate this medium and escalate uncertainty rather than assume isolation.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests OCR text or browser-rendered content from agent_a without sanitization, injection becomes actionable.
IF the two agents are connected by copy-paste, shared files, or an MCP bridge, the attack surface expands.
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of OCR text into prompts.
Strip instructions from OCR output before passing it onward.
Use a fixed schema between agents instead of free text.
Add a human review step for any content that looks like commands.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, which may be sensitive, but system_prompts_leaks shows no data classes touched and no shared workspace or upload path is documented. With no evidence of a shared filesystem or outbound exfiltration from B, leakage is possible only through an external integration not shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are placed on the same shared workspace, file leakage becomes plausible.
IF agent_b is configured to forward received text to a third party, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid placing secrets in OCR input files.
Turn off any automatic export from agent_b.
Review logs for document contents after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser execution, while system_prompts_leaks shows network egress none and no write surfaces. There is no documented overlapping write or mutable-resource capability, so a capability conflict is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory or shared OAuth scope is added later, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources separate.
Do not grant shared OAuth scopes.
Avoid mounting the same directory into both agents.
Recheck the profiles after any capability change.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can emit extracted text that another agent may treat as authoritative, and system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage rather than verification. The pair lacks a documented validation step, so downstream misuse of OCR output is plausible in default integrations even though the exact pipeline is not shown.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output as facts or instructions without verification, cascading error is active.
IF agent_a output is used to trigger actions or summaries, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require a verification step before agent_b acts on OCR output.
Pass structured fields instead of raw text.
Flag low-confidence OCR spans for review.
Limit downstream actions to read-only summaries.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR processes documents and images, so compliance depends on the document class, while system_prompts_leaks has no documented residency, retention, or certification claims. With no explicit mismatch shown, this is a low-risk compliance uncertainty rather than a demonstrated breach; the other agent is not cited for a specific violation because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is fed into agent_a and then exported through agent_b, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency requirements are imposed externally, the pair must be rechecked.
mitigations: Classify input documents before processing.
Exclude regulated data from the workflow.
Document retention for OCR outputs.
Confirm residency and DPA terms for any downstream storage.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing.
